Leveling mortgage insurance premiums to 25 basis points across all multifamily categories is a win for taxpayers and developers. The Green MIP category was classic bureaucratic bloat—tying housing access to ideological checklists while inflating costs. ESG-driven mandates like this are stealth taxes disguised as virtue, forcing builders to prioritize compliance over affordability.

Scrapping annual energy reporting requirements alone will save millions in administrative waste. This reversal aligns with broader efforts to purge D.C.’s obsession with social engineering through regulation.

Affordable housing needs market-driven solutions, not green tape. Next target: the $2.3B HUD “climate resilience” slush fund that diverts resources from actual infrastructure.

HUD’s 90-day foreclosure pause for FHA loans is a start, but let’s not pretend bureaucracy isn’t part of the problem. Over 900 homeowners in Kerr County need real relief, not just temporary freezes. Private lenders like Fairway and Home Depot already stepped up with $1.25M in aid—meanwhile, HUD’s track record on timely disbursements raises questions.

When disaster strikes, agencies love announcing moratoriums but struggle to cut red tape. The real test? Ensuring Section 203(h) loans actually reach families without drowning them in paperwork.

Relief shouldn’t require a miracle—just competence.
